name: Rosewood Hotel Georgia
insider_take: A century-old Vancouver icon reborn — where gilded Jazz Age grandeur meets modern West Coast luxury in the heart of the city.
whats_special: Originally opened in 1927, the Hotel Georgia was Vancouver's most glamorous address, hosting legends like Elvis Presley, Frank Sinatra, and the Rolling Stones. Today, meticulously restored as the Rosewood Hotel Georgia , it retains its stunning Georgian Revival architecture while delivering world-class amenities. The hotel's crown jewel, 1927 Lobby Lounge , pays homage to its storied past with handcrafted cocktails and live jazz. Its rooftop pool and spa offer breathtaking views of the surrounding mountains and city skyline — a rare urban escape right on West Georgia Street , steps from Robson Square and the Vancouver Art Gallery.
pro_tip: Book a corner suite for sweeping panoramic views of both the North Shore Mountains and the vibrant downtown core. Then head down to Hawksworth Restaurant — one of Vancouver's most celebrated dining rooms — for a pre-theater dinner before catching a show at the nearby Queen Elizabeth Theatre.
dont_miss: Don't miss the Sense, A Rosewood Spa , offering signature Pacific Northwest-inspired treatments using locally sourced botanicals. Just outside the hotel doors, explore the seawall path along Stanley Park , one of North America's greatest urban parks, or stroll through the luxury boutiques of Alberni Street — Vancouver's own "Miracle Mile" of high-end shopping.
pros: Historic landmark building with timeless elegance and character
Prime downtown Vancouver location near shopping and attractions
Exceptional personalized service with high staff-to-guest ratio
Award-winning Hawksworth Restaurant with acclaimed Pacific Northwest cuisine
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive positioning
Historic building constraints may limit some modern amenities
